latin: Si spiritus a filio non procederet, a filio non distingueretur.

mentions.context: issues and themes discussed in scholastic philosophy in both the medieval and Renaissance contexts, but also, at times, it shows the difference in motivation, focus and competence between Pico and Thomas. Thesis 1 states that if the Spirit did not proceed from the Son, it would not be distinguished from the Son.5 It can be found in Thomas’s Quaestiones dis- putatae de potentia, q. 10, a. 5, entitled: ‘whether the Holy Spirit would remain distinct from the Son if it did not proceed from Him’ (Utrum spiritus sanctus a
